newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian cabinet to meet Friday on 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Italian cabinet to meet Friday on 1997 budget.

text.p: Italy's centre-left cabinet will meet on Friday to examine the draft 1997 budget, Prime Minister Romano Prodi's office announced on Thursday.

It confirmed the meeting would go ahead despite apparent failure so far to win the support of the hard-left Communist Refoundation party for a tough package seen by Prodi as crucial to Italy's bid to make the grade for a single European currency.

A summit of leaders of parties which back the government, including Communist Refoundation, was postponed on Wednesday to allow more time for negotiations and was expected to be held later on Thursday.
Prodi's government depends on Communist Refoundation for a majority in the lower house of parliament though the party is not part of the government.
The Treasury is now putting the finishing touches to a 1997 budget which Prodi hopes will cut next year's deficit by at least 32.4 trillion lire ($21 billion).

Many economic commentators expect the government to raise the target in the face of worsening 1996 accounts and the need to meet tough deficit criteria if Italy is to be among countries joining a single currency from the planned start in 1999.
